walkthroughs.body_html:
Percentage by mass tells you how much of a sample is one thing.

Formula: (mass of part ÷ total mass) × 100.

Example: a 200 g bottle contains 40 g of recycled plastic. Recycled content = (40 ÷ 200) × 100 = 20%.

Each time you recycle a material, some is lost as waste or contamination.

If a bottle keeps 90% of its mass per recycle, after 2 cycles it has (0.9 × 0.9) = 0.81, so 81% remains.

This is why we say recycling is finite too — not infinite reuse.

Recycling aluminium uses about 5% of the energy needed to extract it from ore by electrolysis.

So if making 1 kg of new aluminium needs 200 MJ, recycling 1 kg only needs about 10 MJ.

That's a 95% energy saving — a huge LCA win.
